Start from `origin/main` (`git fetch origin` first; if blocked use existing refs); branch `fix/weekly-oracle-measurement`; commit locally; I push and open the PR. Read /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/worker-contract.md (incl. 'no new scripts/options/recipes unless wired into CI/weekly'), /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/oracle-run/REPORT.md (Quality and 'What failed' sections), docs/measurement.md, scripts/weekly.py, scripts/headline.py, scripts/oracle_data.py, scripts/test_weekly*.py, scripts/test_headline.py, .github/workflows/weekly.yml, apps/oracle/. Problems to fix: (1) the oracle step runs out of Node heap on Chakra (default ~4 GB: exit 134) and needs `REDACTED` (the rerun passed with it: 620 components, 486,834 props, exit 0); set it where the oracle is spawned (scripts/weekly.py / oracle_data.py, and any CI step), sized by a named constant with a comment on the measured need, and make a memory failure of a step a recorded `failed` entry with the log tail, not a silent absence. (2) the headline reads Chakra 16.7% and Mantine 32.7% correct because 75.5% / 62.9% of props are 'not judged' (0 wrong): the single 'correct %' hides that the oracle did not check most props. Report `not judged` as its own first-class column next to correct / less precise / wrong in the weekly markdown and the issue text, define the headline rate over JUDGED props (correct / (correct + less precise + wrong), with the denominator shown) AND show coverage = judged / total, and gate on both (the existing gate on wrong props stays; add a documented floor on coverage only if the data supports one: look at the stored records and the reports; if not, report it without a gate and say so). In headline.py keep the old fields so earlier records compare; bump UNIVERSE_VERSION or REFERENCE_VERSION only if the meaning of a stored field changes (see their comments), and say why. (3) the weekly's recall vs RDT counts `@types/react` props as 'recalled' by listed props, but with the checker on the whole-project merge keeps React's props in the element layer (and with PR 490 the layer carries the names): measured recall of `@types/react` props is 0.4% (Mantine), about 0% (Chakra), 4.9% (shadcn), 23.9% (antd), 86.8% (Spectrum) versus 99% on 0.10.0 (no checker). Count a React prop as recalled when it is listed OR named in an inheritance layer's members (the JSON carries `nameLists`; look at how recall reads `own_layers`/`react_layers` in weekly.py: the record already has `react_layers`), and report both the listed and the layered recall so the column measures information kept, not rows. Check docs/measurement.md's description of the column and update it. (4) the CI weekly of 2026-11-15 died with exit 143 on 'chakra: Caliper' (a kill; memory on 0.11.0); with the memory fixes in main this should pass: add nothing for it, but make sure STEP_TIMEOUT/failed handling reports a signal death clearly (read the code; fix only if unclear). Tests first: scripts/test_weekly.py / test_headline.py cases for each change (python3 -I -m unittest or the project's runner: see the justfile `test-py`), including a record with not_judged > 0 and a record from before (missing fields). Keep changes small and in the existing files. Gates: `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `just test-py`, `just semver` if a changeset is demanded (these are scripts: probably none; check the AGENTS.md changeset rule: only consumer-visible changes). Do NOT run the oracle itself (costs money; the lead runs it). Cap 50 tool calls. Notes to /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/fix-weekly-oracle-measurement.md (## What, ## Evidence, ## Not verified, session URL line). Final message at most 60 words: SHA, exit codes, what the headline shows for a record with Chakra's numbers (16.7% / 75.5% not judged).

# Worker contract (caliper). Read once; the brief only names the task, the files you own and the call cap.

Scope
- Edit only the files the brief names. If another file must change, stop and say which and why.
- Never ask the user questions. If blocked, report what blocks and what you tried. Do not wait on background work: finish or report.

Branch and push
- Branch from origin/main unless the brief says otherwise. Own CARGO_TARGET_DIR under ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/<task>/. Scratch there too, never /tmp.
- Rust 1.99.1 on PATH (/Users/gabe/.rustup/toolchains/1.99.1-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin) for builds; commits need MISE_RUST_VERSION=1.99.1 (the mise shim forces 1.98.1). Caveat: with the toolchain bin first on PATH `rust-objcopy` can fail and strip silently does nothing; irrelevant unless you measure binary size.
- Signed commits ending `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013R2ytvK9B32ZaSUaSe6aAZ`. Push normally (`git push origin HEAD:<branch>`), never --no-verify, verify the remote SHA with `git ls-remote`. Do not open or edit the PR, do not poll CI.

Checks: targeted, CI runs the rest
- Always, before push: `just lint doc-check machete typos` (fast).
- Then only what your change touches: Rust -> nextest of the touched crates; types/output/merge -> `just test-checker-lane` once; checker/session code -> gate_harness determinism and memory modes; output-preserving change -> full-content diff (JSON parsed, `stats` dropped) of `extract --json --quiet --no-cache` vs a build of origin/main on ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large/src and ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/checker-default/chakra-only/src (tools: ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/perf-analysis/same.py, identity.sh; ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/final-perf/ab.sh interleaves two binaries).
- Do NOT run deny, semver, test-ts, test-napi, test-integration, test-py unless you changed those areas: CI runs them on every PR.
- Tests that fail on base for every behavior change. No oracle runs, no corpus fetches. No new scripts, options or recipes. Changeset only if `just semver` demands one.
- No wall-clock timing unless the brief asks; check `uptime`, and prefer allocation or instruction counts (load-independent).

Cap
- Stop and report after the call cap in the brief (default 60 tool calls) with what you have verified. Listing something as 'not done' with its cause beats burning more calls.

Artifacts (agents to agents; humans see them at the edge)
- Write the PR body to ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/<branch, slashes as dashes>.md: `## What`, `## Evidence` (numbers, exit codes, what was diffed), `## Not verified`, last line `https://claude.ai/code/session_013R2ytvK9B32ZaSUaSe6aAZ`. The lead publishes it unedited.
- Final message <= 120 words: branch, head SHA (ls-remote verified), body path, blockers. Nothing else.

Pre-push gate (the reviewer must find nothing new; read ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/findings-synthesis.md, classes C1-C8)
- Guards are ALLOW-lists: handle a closed set of proven forms, everything else is Unknown/Declined (never 'complete', never 'none', never 'exact'). No `_ =>` arms in decisions over node/type kinds.
- Write the slice's invariants in the PR body (unknown unless proven; by binding not spelling; every read recorded; one owner; wired or not defined).
- Grammar sweep: list every syntax/type form the code can receive and show each is handled or declined (exhaustive match, or a generated test over the grammar with the checker/TS API as oracle). Generate over the GRAMMAR, not over past findings.
- Mutation proof: remove each guard/dependency; a test must fail. Report which you tried.
- Before reporting: run `/code-review medium` on your explicit SHA range, then try to break your own change with inputs the diff did not mention (computed keys, symbols, getters, overloads, re-exports, shadowing, optional chains, declare/abstract, conditional types).

## Storybook dev mode

|---|---|---|---|

| Restart with cache kept, Button (edited before the restart: not a pure cache hit) | 889 ms | 1,264 ms, structural (+375 ms) | 1,370 ms (+106 ms) |
| Restart with cache kept, Input first visit | 895 ms | 1,040 ms (+145 ms), 445 rows | n/a |

Memory: the Storybook node process 893 MiB RSS, plus esbuild 16 + 61 MiB and the npm wrapper 92 MiB; no separate checker process. Row content: the collapsed `SystemProperties` layer does not appear as rows (no `bg`, `p`, `m`), but the DOM and condition props do. The roughly 146 figure was not reproduced. Versus the earlier 0.11.0 demo: rows 1,141 to 437; structural-to-checker swap 154 ms to 134 ms.

## vs 0.11.0

No stored 0.11.0 weekly record exists (the CI weekly of 2026-11-15, run 43686845177, died with exit 143 on "chakra: Caliper"; the last green record is 2026-11-09, 0.10.0 with `--no-checker` on a GitHub runner, not comparable). From docs/measurement.md (0.11 plus the PR 468 fix): Chakra then 4.5 s / 6.9 GB, now 3.5 s / 1.9 GB (time -22%, memory -72%); the other four within 0.1 s and 0.05 GB. 0.11.0 as released needed 42 GB on Chakra. Headline vs 0.10.0 (older universe, no checker): Mantine 93.6% to 32.7% (the gap is "not judged"; 0 wrong both times), shadcn 94.2% to 98.7%, antd 94.2% to 93.0%, Spectrum 83.8% to 88.4% (1,032 components vs 454).

## What failed or was not measured

- Chakra oracle: OOM at the default Node heap (log tail in `logs/weekly.log`); a rerun with `REDACTED` was unfinished at hand-back.
- A quiet machine was never reached (load 5 to 10).
- Neighbour vs distant story with prefetch: not measured. antd in Storybook: Vite fails with `Failed to resolve import "./version"` (generated file). No big Mantine or antd story measured. Not recorded: warm-restart ready time, RDT's dev-server cost, a Badge screenshot.
- Cold run clears only Caliper's cache directory; the OS file cache was warm.
- Not diagnosed: the @types/react recall drop and the 437 rows. Both look like checker-mode output omitting or not collapsing DOM props (ADR 0028 "ambient" props); not checked whether that is intended.

"""The data files of apps/oracle/src that the scripts read as the oracle does: the vocabulary of its verdicts
(vocabulary.json, written from vocabulary.ts), the shape rules (component-shape.json) and the path classes
(path-classes.json). scripts/test_oracle_data.py, test_component_shape.py and test_path_classes.py run the oracle's cases
against them, so a rule changed on one side only fails a test."""
import json
import os
import re

ORACLE_SRC = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), 'apps', 'oracle', 'src')


def read(name):
    with open(os.path.join(ORACLE_SRC, name)) as f:
        return json.load(f)


VOCABULARY = read('vocabulary.json')
SHAPE = read('component-shape.json')
PATHS = read('path-classes.json')

VERDICTS = VOCABULARY['verdicts']
AGREE = VOCABULARY['agree']

DEPENDENCY = re.compile(PATHS['dependency'])
REACT_TYPES = re.compile(PATHS['reactTypes'])
LIB_FILE = re.compile(PATHS['libFile'])


def _slashed(path):
    return path.replace('\\', '/')


def is_dependency(path):
    """Whether the file is installed under a `node_modules` directory, `@types/react` and the lib files included."""
    return bool(DEPENDENCY.search(_slashed(path)))


def is_react_types(path):
    """Whether the file is part of `@types/react`."""
    return bool(REACT_TYPES.search(_slashed(path)))


def is_lib_file(path):
    """Whether the file is one of TypeScript's `lib.*.d.ts`."""
    return bool(LIB_FILE.search(_slashed(path)))
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The weekly headline: how correct the types are that Storybook and agents are shown, and when to open an issue.

The headline is read from what the oracle already measured (apps/oracle/src/tool-universe.ts `caliper_reported`): every
own prop TypeScript 7.1's checker finds on a component Caliper reports, each judged against the checker. A prop is
correct (the same type, or the same type spelled differently), less precise (vaguer than the checker's, not
contradicting it), wrong (describing something else), without a checker type (the checker has none either), not judged
(the oracle did not evaluate the checker's type, so nothing was compared), missing (Caliper reports the component but
not the prop), or named only (Caliper lists it by name as a member of a collapsed inheritance layer, so it is surfaced
but has no type to judge).

This module holds the arithmetic and the issue conditions so scripts/weekly.py only calls it. Matching react-docgen-
typescript (recall) is information, never a gate.
"""
import oracle_data

# The gate. Of the props Caliper lists whose type can be judged against the checker's, more than this share wrong opens
# an issue, and so does any rise from the last record: a wrong type in Storybook is the one thing a reader cannot see.
WRONG_GATE = 0.001

# Budgets for one whole run (process start included) of the checker, the default, over a pinned corpus with dependencies
# loaded, per corpus: `ms` and `rss_mib`. They are "something is badly wrong" limits, not tuning: 4 times the time and 2
# times the peak memory measured on the fixed build (docs/measurement.md, "The budgets"), since a CI runner is slower
# and smaller than the machine that measured. The `corpora-budget` job of the Callisto release pull request fails on
# one, and the weekly opens its issue. They are not week-over-week limits: a shared CI machine drifts by 10% or more on
# its own, and a drift that stays inside the budget is not a problem.
BUDGETS = {
    'chakra': {'ms': 18000, 'rss_mib': 14336},
    'mantine': {'ms': 4000, 'rss_mib': 2048},

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The weekly record: Caliper, react-docgen-typescript (RDT) and react-docgen on the five pinned corpora.

For each corpus it records, per tool, the wall time and peak RSS of one whole run (process start included), and for
Caliper the canonical JSON's size. Recall is measured against RDT: of the components RDT reports with props, how many
the tool also reports (same file, same name), and of their props, how many it lists, split into the props `@types/react`
declares and the rest. react-docgen follows imports to the file that declares a type but infers nothing, and lists none
of React's props. With --oracle it also records how often TypeScript 7.1's checker contradicts each tool's prop types,
over every prop the checker finds, and the headline of scripts/headline.py: how many of the props of the components Caliper
reports are right. With --agent-eval it also asks a fixed list of questions about real components and scores what a
reader of Caliper's output answers against the checker (scripts/agent_eval.py).

--previous FILE compares with an earlier record (the last green run's artifact) and writes --issue FILE for the workflow
to open or update one issue with, when a wrong type is above the gate or rises, a reader's question is answered
silent-wrong, or a whole run is over a budget (scripts/headline.py). Drift in time, memory and recall against RDT is
listed in the summary, not alarmed on.

Every measured command's exit status and wall time go to stderr, and --out is written after each corpus. A corpus whose
command exits non-zero, dies of a signal or runs past STEP_TIMEOUT is recorded under `failed` (step, exit status, last
20 lines of stderr) and the next corpus still runs; the exit status is 1 at the end if any failed. --enforce-budgets
also exits 1 when a whole run is over its corpus's budget: the `corpora-budget` job of the release pull request.

Usage: scripts/weekly.py --bin BIN [--corpus NAME]... [--corpora DIR] [--work DIR] [--runs N] [--oracle] [--agent-eval]
                         [--previous FILE] [--baseline-failed] [--enforce-budgets] [--out FILE] [--markdown FILE] [--issue FILE]
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

import agent_eval
import corpora
import headline
import oracle_data
import schema_version
from corpora import ROOT, run_once, selected

BASELINE_FAILED = "The baseline download failed, so this run was not compared with last week's record."
SLOWER = 1.10
RECALL_DROP = 0.02
# The rules that decide what the reference is: the exclusions and the pairing. Raise it when a change to them moves recall,
# so that a record is never compared on recall with one made under other rules (a record without it is version 1).
REFERENCE_VERSION = 3
# The universe of the oracle's scores (`oracle.tools`): version 2 counts candidate components only, naming a default export
# by its declaration; a record without it is version 1, which counted every function the checker takes for a component
# and named a default export `default`. Version 3 pairs a checker component with Caliper's by file and export name
# (ADR 0027) where version 2 paired by a normalised display name. Version 4 scores a prop whose checker type the oracle did
# not evaluate as `not judged` where version 3 scored it identical, and classes a declaration's path by one rule
# (apps/oracle/src/path-classes.json). Version 5 extracts with the checker, the default, where version 4 and earlier ran
# `--no-checker`, so the oracle's props and verdicts are not the same measurement. Raise it when a change moves what the
# oracle counts.
UNIVERSE_VERSION = 5
# No single measured command runs longer than this (seconds): a hung one is killed and its corpus recorded as failed.
STEP_TIMEOUT = 2400


class StepFailed(Exception):
    """A command of one corpus's measurement that did not finish well: `step` names it, `code` is its exit status
    (negative for a signal, None for a timeout) and `tail` the last 20 lines of its stderr."""

    def __init__(self, step, message, code=None, tail=''):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.step = step
        self.code = code
        self.tail = tail


def log(message):
    print(message, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)


def step(label, command, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=None):
    """`run_once` of one measured command, logging its exit status and wall time to stderr; a command that fails is a
    StepFailed naming `label`."""
    start = time.monotonic()
    try:
        result = run_once(command, stdout=stdout, timeout=STEP_TIMEOUT if timeout is None else timeout)
    except corpora.RunFailed as error:
        log(f'{label}: exit {error.code if error.code is not None else "none"} after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s: {error}')
        raise StepFailed(label, str(error), error.code, error.tail) from error
    log(f'{label}: exit 0 after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s')
    return result


def capture(label, command, timeout=None):
    """The stdout of a command that must succeed, logged like `step`."""
    start = time.monotonic()
    try:
        done = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, errors='replace',
                              timeout=STEP_TIMEOUT if timeout is None else timeout)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:
        log(f'{label}: timed out after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s')
        raise StepFailed(label, f'{label} ran past its {error.timeout} s timeout and was killed') from error
    except OSError as error:
        log(f'{label}: cannot run: {error}')
        raise StepFailed(label, f'{label}: cannot run: {error}', 127) from error
    log(f'{label}: exit {done.returncode} after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s')
    if done.returncode != 0:
        raise StepFailed(label, f'{label} exited with {done.returncode}', done.returncode,
                         '\n'.join(done.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-20:]))
    return done.stdout


def norm_name(name):
    """A component name as the tools may spell it: no `(file)` suffix, namespace or punctuation."""
    name = re.sub(r' \(.*\)$', '', name).split('/')[-1].split('.')[-1]
    return re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]', '', name.lower())


def relative(path, root):
    """`path` relative to `root`, both through symlinks: Caliper reports canonical paths, RDT the ones it was given."""
    return os.path.relpath(os.path.realpath(path), os.path.realpath(root))


def program_inputs(name, src, out_dir):
    """The component files (every `.tsx` under the source directory) and a tsconfig rooted there."""
    files = []
    for current, dirs, names in os.walk(src):
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d != 'node_modules']
        files += [os.path.join(current, n) for n in names if n.endswith('.tsx')]
    list_file = os.path.join(out_dir, f'{name}.files.txt')
    with open(list_file, 'w') as f:
        f.write('\n'.join(sorted(files)) + '\n')
    tsconfig = os.path.join(out_dir, f'{name}.tsconfig.json')
    with open(tsconfig, 'w') as f:
        json.dump({
            'include': [f'{src}/**/*.ts', f'{src}/**/*.tsx'],
            'compilerOptions': {'target': 'ES2022', 'module': 'ESNext', 'moduleResolution': 'bundler', 'jsx': 'react-jsx',
                                'strict': True, 'skipLibCheck': True, 'noEmit': True},
        }, f, indent=2)
    return list_file, tsconfig


def tool_run(command, out, label='tool'):
    """One whole run of a Node tool that writes its components to `out`: wall ms, peak RSS MiB and the components."""
    seconds, rss = step(label, command)
    with open(out) as f:
        return {'ms': round(seconds * 1000), 'rss_mib': round(rss)}, json.load(f)['components']


def caliper_run(binary, src, runs, label='Caliper'):
    """Median wall ms and largest peak RSS MiB of `extract --json` in the Storybook addon's configuration (dependencies
    loaded, `--collapse-inherited-props dependencies` pinned: the addon's default), and the JSON's size. The checker answers, as
    it does by default (docs/measurement.md). The parse caches are warm (a warm-up run fills them), but each timed run
    asks the checker everything: the answer `extract` keeps is removed first, since react-docgen-typescript keeps none.
    `rerun_ms` is the median of as many runs that find it, what a rerun over unchanged files costs."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as cache, tempfile.TemporaryFile() as out:
        command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'dependencies',
                   '--cache-dir', cache]
        step(f'{label} warm-up', command, stdout=out)
        size = out.tell()
        kept = os.path.join(cache, 'checker-answers.msgpack')
        samples = []
        for _ in range(runs):
            if os.path.exists(kept):
                os.remove(kept)
            samples.append(step(f'{label} run {len(samples) + 1}', command))
        reruns = [step(f'{label} rerun {i + 1}', command) for i in range(runs)]
    return {'ms': round(statistics.median(s for s, _ in samples) * 1000), 'rss_mib': round(max(r for _, r in samples)),
            'json_mb': round(size / 2**20, 2), 'rerun_ms': round(statistics.median(s for s, _ in reruns) * 1000)}


def caliper_components(binary, src, root, label='Caliper components'):
    """Caliper's components in RDT's format, as (file, name) -> prop names."""
    command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--format', 'rdt', '--html-attributes', 'full', '--include-unexported',
               '--quiet', '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'none']
    out = capture(label, command)
    return {(relative(c['filePath'], root), norm_name(c['displayName'])): set(c['props'])
            for c in json.loads(out[out.index('{'):]).values()}


def caliper_layer_members(binary, src, root, label='Caliper layers'):
    """The props Caliper's collapsed inheritance layers hold, as (file, name) -> prop names: the output names them in a
    layer instead of listing them as props, and the canonical JSON is the one that carries the layers."""
    command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--html-attributes', 'full', '--include-unexported', '--quiet',
               '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'none']
    out = capture(label, command)
    document = schema_version.check(json.loads(out[out.index('{'):]), 'weekly')
    lists = document.get('nameLists', {})
    members = {}
    for c in document['components'].values():
        names = set()
        for layer in c.get('inheritance', []):
            if layer.get('members'):
                names |= set(lists[layer['members']])
        members[(relative(c['filePath'], root), norm_name(c['displayName']))] = names
    return members


# The shape rules of `exclusion`, shared with the oracle's universe (apps/oracle/src/component-shape.ts): the patterns are in
# one file both read (scripts/oracle_data.py), and both run the cases of apps/oracle/tests/fixtures/component-shape-cases.json.
HOOK = re.compile(oracle_data.SHAPE['hook'])
PROMISE_TYPE = re.compile(oracle_data.SHAPE['promiseType'])
EXTENSIONS = ('', '.tsx', '.ts', '/index.tsx', '/index.ts')
# An identifier inside any number of calls (`memo(forwardRef(Foo))`, `React.memo(Foo)`, `Object.assign(Foo, {...})`),
# followed by what ends an argument or an expression: `, ) ; !`, a type assertion or the end of the line.
WRAPPED = r'(?:[\w.]+\s*(?:<[^>]*>)?\s*\(\s*)*(\w+)(?=\s*[,);!]|\s+as\b|\s+satisfies\b|\s*$)'


def declared_in_react(info):
    return oracle_data.is_react_types(info.get('parent') or '')


def exclusion(comp):
    """Why RDT's entry is not a component, from what RDT reports about it, or None. RDT lists every function it can
    give a parameter to, so hooks, route handlers, helpers and context objects come with it. The evidence is the shape:
    props that are the members of a TypeScript lib type (`String`, `Function`, `Request`) mean the parameter is not an
    object of props; a hook is named `use` and a capital; a `value` declared by `@types/react` and nothing else is a
    context's Provider; a lowercase name cannot be a JSX tag unless it takes the attributes of one (a `@types/react`
    prop) or is the file's or directory's own name, which RDT gives a default export; and props that are all promises
    are handed over by a router, not by a parent. The oracle's universe applies the same rules to the checker's functions
    (apps/oracle/src/component-shape.ts)."""
    props = comp['props']
    in_lib = sum(oracle_data.is_lib_file(i.get('parent') or '') for i in props.values())
    if in_lib * 2 > len(props):
        return 'lib_members'
    name = comp['name']
    if HOOK.search(name):
        return 'hook'
    if 'value' in props and set(props) <= set(oracle_data.SHAPE['contextValueProps']) and all(map(declared_in_react, props.values())):
        return 'context_value'
    if name[:1].islower() and norm_name(name) not in own_names(comp['file']) and not any(map(declared_in_react, props.values())):
        return 'not_jsx'
    if all(PROMISE_TYPE.search(i.get('type', '')) for i in props.values()):
        return 'promise_props'
    return None


def read_text(path):
    """A source file's text, or None if there is no such file."""
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return None
    with open(path, errors='replace') as f:
        return f.read()


def import_binding(text, name):
    """Where `name` was imported from in `text`: (module, imported name) or None."""
    for match in re.finditer(r"^import\s+(?:type\s+)?([^;'\"]*?)\s+from\s+['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"]", text, re.M):
        clause, module = match.groups()
        if not clause.startswith('{'):
            default, _, clause = clause.partition(',')
            if default.strip() == name:
                return module, 'default'
        for original, alias in re.findall(r'(\w+)(?:\s+as\s+(\w+))?', clause.partition('{')[2].partition('}')[0]):
            if (alias or original) == name:
                return module, original
    return None


def export_source(text, name):
    """How `text` exports `name` (`default` or a name): ('local', local name), ('from', module, name) or None."""
    if name == 'default':
        # The second pattern unwraps calls whose first argument is an identifier (`memo(Foo)`, `observer(forwardRef(Foo))`,
        # `Object.assign(Foo, {...})`), and a trailing assertion (`Foo as T`, `Foo satisfies T`, `Foo!`): the wrapper is
        # whatever function the file calls, so the name that matters is the innermost identifier.
        for pattern in (r'^export\s+default\s+(?:async\s+)?(?:function\*?|class)\s+(\w+)',
                        rf'^export\s+default\s+{WRAPPED}'):
            match = re.search(pattern, text, re.M)
            if match:
                return 'local', match.group(1)
    else:
        declaration = rf'^export\s+(?:declare\s+)?(?:const|let|var|function\*?|class|async\s+function)\s+{re.escape(name)}\b'
        if re.search(declaration, text, re.M):
            return 'local', name
    for match in re.finditer(r"^export\s*\{([^}]*)\}\s*(?:from\s*['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"])?", text, re.M):
        for original, alias in re.findall(r'(\w+)(?:\s+as\s+(\w+))?', match.group(1)):
            if (alias or original) == name:
                return ('from', match.group(2), original) if match.group(2) else ('local', original)
    return None


def export_aliases(text, local):
    """The names `text` exports the local binding `local` under, other than its own (`export { _Card as Card }`)."""
    names = []
    for match in re.finditer(r"^export\s*\{([^}]*)\}\s*(?!from)", text or '', re.M):
        names += [alias for original, alias in re.findall(r'(\w+)\s+as\s+(\w+)', match.group(1)) if original == local]
    return names


def resolve_module(file, module, exists):
    """The file `module` names from `file` (relative paths only), as a path relative to the root."""
    if not module.startswith('.'):
        return None
    base = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(file), module))
    return next((base + ext for ext in EXTENSIONS if exists(base + ext)), None)


def export_target(file, read, exists, name='default', hops=6):
    """The file and local name where what `file` exports as `name` is defined: follows `export default X`,
    `import X from`, `export { X } from` and `export { default as X }` through re-exports. None where it ends elsewhere."""
    text = read(file)
    exported = export_source(text, name) if text and hops else None
    if not exported:
        return None
    if exported[0] == 'from':
        target = resolve_module(file, exported[1], exists)
        return export_target(target, read, exists, exported[2], hops - 1) if target else None
    chain = local_chain(text, exported[1])
    for local in chain:
        imported = import_binding(text, local)
        if imported:
            target = resolve_module(file, imported[0], exists)
            return export_target(target, read, exists, imported[1], hops - 1) if target else None
    return file, exported[1]


def local_chain(text, name, hops=4):
    """`name` and what a chain of `const name = Other` / `const name = memo(Other)` in `text` leads to, nearest first:
    the component is declared under the last, and Caliper may report it under any of them."""
    names = [name]
    while text and len(names) <= hops:
        match = re.search(rf'^(?:export\s+)?(?:const|let|var)\s+{re.escape(names[-1])}\b(?:\s*:[^=\n]+)?\s*=\s*{WRAPPED}',
                          text, re.M)
        if not match or match.group(1) in names:
            break
        names.append(match.group(1))
    return names


def display_assignments(text):
    """The `Foo.displayName = 'Bar'` assignments in `text`, as (local name, shown name) pairs."""
    return re.findall(r"^\s*(\w+)\.displayName\s*=\s*['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"]", text or '', re.M)


def own_names(file):
    """The names RDT gives a default export of `file`: the file's own, and its directory's."""
    return {norm_name(os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(file))[0]), norm_name(os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(file)))}


def counterpart(file, name, found_by_file, read=None, claimed=()):
    """Caliper's key in `file` for a component called `name`, or None: the names must agree, since a file's only
    component says nothing about whether RDT's entry is that component. With `read`, the names a local alias chain
    leads to count too, and the `displayName` each is given; a key in `claimed` (one an RDT entry already matches
    exactly) is never the answer."""
    text = read(file) if read else None
    names = local_chain(text, name) if read else [name]
    # Caliper names a component by its `displayName` where there is one, RDT by the declaration.
    shown = dict(display_assignments(text))
    for candidate in [n for local in names for n in (local, shown.get(local)) if n]:
        key = (file, norm_name(candidate))
        if norm_name(candidate) in found_by_file.get(file, {}) and key not in claimed:
            return key
    return None


def pair(comp, root, found_by_file, read, exists, claimed=()):
    """Caliper's key and the evidence for RDT's entry that Caliper does not report under its own key. In another file:
    where the default export of RDT's file is defined (RDT names a default export after the file or directory) or, for a
    named export, where that is. In the same file: the component that default export is, when the RDT name is the file's
    or directory's own and no other entry already matches it, or the one whose `displayName` RDT reports. Else the file
    that declares its props, when Caliper reports a component of that name there. A local alias chain
    (`const A = memo(B); export default A`) leads to the declaration. None if no evidence leads to a component."""
    file = relative(comp['file'], root)
    for export in ('default', comp['name']):
        target = export_target(file, read, exists, export)
        if not target:
            continue
        if target[0] != file:
            found = counterpart(target[0], target[1], found_by_file, read)
            if found:
                return found, 'default_export' if export == 'default' else 'named_export'
        elif export == 'default' and norm_name(comp['name']) in own_names(file):
            found = counterpart(file, target[1], found_by_file, read, claimed)
            if found:
                return found, 'default_alias'
    local = next((l for l, shown in display_assignments(read(file)) if norm_name(shown) == norm_name(comp['name'])), None)
    found = counterpart(file, local, found_by_file, read, claimed) if local else None
    if found:
        return found, 'display_name'
    # Caliper names a component exported under another name (`export { _Card as Card }`) by the export name, RDT by the declaration.
    for alias in export_aliases(read(file), comp['name']):
        found = counterpart(file, alias, found_by_file, read, claimed)
        if found:
            return found, 'export_alias'
    name = norm_name(comp['name'])
    for info in comp['props'].values():
        parent = info.get('parent') or ''
        declared = relative(parent, root) if parent and not oracle_data.is_react_types(parent) else None
        if declared and declared != file and name in found_by_file.get(declared, {}):
            return (declared, name), 'declaration'
    return None


LIST_CAP = 15


def from_dependency(text, name):
    """Whether `text` imports `name` from a package (any form of import), not from a relative path."""
    for match in re.finditer(r"^import\s+(?:type\s+)?([^;'\"]*?)\s+from\s+['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"]", text, re.M):
        if not match.group(2).startswith('.') and re.search(rf'\b{re.escape(name)}\b', match.group(1)):
            return True
    return False


def reaches_dependency(file, read, exists, name, hops=6):
    """Whether what `file` exports as `name` ends in a package: `export { X } from 'pkg'`, or an import from one."""

def unmatched_cause(name, file, found_by_file, read, exists):
    """Why Caliper reports none of an item's names, from the item's file: a member of another component
    (`Form.List = List`); a member of an object literal (`logo: () => ...`); an alias of something a package exports
    (`const Tooltip = Recharts.Tooltip`); a value a call builds (`createIcon(...)`, `generateCalendar(...)`); a name the
    file exports from a package; else a component the file declares that Caliper does not report, in a file where it
    reports others or none. RDT names a default export after the file, so for that name the declaration is the one the
    default export leads to. The causes are what the file shows, so a cause says where to look, not what is wrong."""
    text = read(file) or ''
    names = [name.split('.')[-1]]
    default = norm_name(name) in own_names(file)
    exported = export_source(text, 'default') if default else None
    if exported and exported[0] == 'local':
        names += local_chain(text, exported[1])
    pattern = '(?:' + '|'.join(map(re.escape, dict.fromkeys(names))) + ')'
    declaration = rf'^(?:export\s+)?(?:const|let|var)\s+{pattern}\b(?:\s*:[^=\n]+)?\s*=\s*'
    if re.search(rf'\b\w+\.{pattern}\s*=[^=]', text):
        return 'compound_member'
    if re.search(rf'^\s+{pattern}\s*:\s*(?:\(|<|function\b|async\b|[\w$]+\s*=>|(?:React\.)?(?:memo|forwardRef)\b)', text, re.M):
        return 'object_member'
    alias = re.search(declaration + r'(\w+)(?:\.\w+)*\s*;?\s*$', text, re.M)
    if alias and from_dependency(text, alias.group(1)):
        return 'dependency'
    if re.search(declaration + r'[\w.]+\s*(?:<[^>]*>)?\(', text, re.M):
        return 'call_result'
    if reaches_dependency(file, read, exists, name) or (default and reaches_dependency(file, read, exists, 'default')):
        return 'dependency'
    return 'file_with_other_components' if found_by_file.get(file) else 'file_without_components'


def reference(rdt_components, found, root):
    """The components recall is measured on, from RDT's output: entries with props, minus those that are not components
    (`exclusion`), with every RDT entry for one component counted once. An entry that Caliper reports under another file
    pairs with it by evidence (`pair`) and joins the entry in that file; RDT's repeats of one key join too. Each item is
    {'keys': every (file, name) a tool may report it under, 'props': prop -> 'own' | 'react'}, so one list serves every
    tool. Also the counts, so a change in the reference shows in weekly.json, and the items Caliper reports nowhere, by
    cause (`unmatched_cause`): a count per cause and the first `LIST_CAP` of each, as `file: name`."""
    found_by_file = {}
    for file, name in found:
        found_by_file.setdefault(file, {})[name] = None
    exists = lambda rel: os.path.isfile(os.path.join(root, rel))
    read = lambda rel: read_text(os.path.join(root, rel))
    stats = {'rdt_with_props': 0, 'excluded': {}, 'exact': 0, 'paired': {}, 'merged': 0}
    entries = []
    for comp in rdt_components:
        if not comp['props']:
            continue
        stats['rdt_with_props'] += 1
        why = exclusion(comp)
        if why:
            stats['excluded'][why] = stats['excluded'].get(why, 0) + 1
            continue
        entries.append((comp, (relative(comp['file'], root), norm_name(comp['name']))))
    # Caliper's keys that an RDT entry matches exactly: another entry in that file is never paired with them.
    claimed = {key for _, key in entries if key in found}
    groups = {}
    for comp, key in entries:
        target = key if key in found else None
        if target:
            stats['exact'] += 1
        else:
            paired = pair(comp, root, found_by_file, read, exists, claimed)
            if paired:
                target = paired[0]
                stats['paired'][paired[1]] = stats['paired'].get(paired[1], 0) + 1
        keys = [key] + ([target] if target else [])
        group = groups.get(target or key)
        if group is None:
            group = groups[target or key] = {'keys': [], 'exact': {}, 'other': {}, 'file': key[0], 'name': comp['name']}
        else:
            stats['merged'] += 1
        group['keys'] += keys
        # The props of the entries in the component's own file when there are any, else of all the repeats united, so the
        # reference does not depend on the order RDT lists them in. A prop any repeat takes from `@types/react` is one.
        into = group['exact' if key == target else 'other']

    return items, stats

With `--oracle` the run also asks TypeScript 7.1's checker (`apps/oracle/src/oracle.ts`, `typescript-beta/sync`, the `7.1.0-beta` package) for each prop's type and compares it structurally with Caliper's canonical `--json`, extracted with `--html-attributes full --include-unexported --load-dependencies --collapse-inherited-props none`: the comparison keeps every prop expanded, as RDT lists them, so recall and the oracle counts stay comparable week to week. Only the timed run follows the addon's configuration, with `--collapse-inherited-props dependencies` pinned (the series steps at this change: before it the timed run expanded every inherited prop). The weekly table shows the share of props that agree (identical, or the same type spelled by name) and the share the checker contradicts, for Caliper, RDT and react-docgen, and the headline below. `agree` is the loose number; `wrong` is the one that matters and the one the weekly issue gates on, but the comparator has artifacts that make it both over- and under-report. `docs/rdt-differences.md` lists every class of disagreement with an example, how it is counted and whether the comparator scored it right. The checker is a beta, so a disagreement is a reason to look, not a verdict on its own. The weekly extracts with the default, the checker, so from `oracle.universe_version` 5 this compares the checker's own answer, merged over the structural one, with the checker's: it agrees almost by construction, and a `wrong` there is a prop the merge changed or kept structural against the checker (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`). The structural resolver alone was judged until version 4.
116:A not judged prop is neither agreement nor a difference. Before `oracle.universe_version` 4 the comparison scored it identical, so a type the checker side never read counted as right. A part of a type that is not judged (an array of an unevaluated element) makes the whole not judged unless another part already differs, in which case the difference wins. The verdict names, their order and which of them agree are one definition, `apps/oracle/src/vocabulary.ts`, written to `apps/oracle/src/vocabulary.json` (`pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle vocabulary`) for `scripts/weekly.py` and `scripts/headline.py` to read; `apps/oracle/tests/vocabulary.test.ts` fails while the two differ. Caliper's own side (`apps/oracle/src/caliper-norm.ts`) is typed against the published `PropType` (`packages/napi/index.d.ts`) with a case for every kind, so a kind added there fails the type check, and a kind a build does not know throws instead of comparing as opaque.
122:The **universe** is every own prop the checker finds on an exported function whose only parameter, or `props` parameter, is the props type, and which can be a component. React's inherited DOM attributes, `ref` and `key` are not in it. The checker has no notion of a component, so a function is left out when its shape says it is none, by the rules that clean the reference for recall (the table above): more than half of its props are declared in TypeScript's `lib.*.d.ts` (the parameter is an `Element` or a `String`), its name is a hook's, its only props are a context Provider's `value` and `children`, its name starts lowercase and is no tag's (not the file's or directory's name, no `@types/react` prop), or every prop is a `Promise`. The rules are one definition: `apps/oracle/src/component-shape.json` holds the patterns, `apps/oracle/src/component-shape.ts` applies them to the checker's functions, `scripts/weekly.py` `exclusion` to RDT's entries, and both run the cases of `apps/oracle/tests/fixtures/component-shape-cases.json`, so they cannot drift apart. The paths those rules read, and the oracle's own (where the checker declares a prop, which declarations are `@types/react`'s), are classed by one file, `apps/oracle/src/path-classes.json` (a dependency is anything under `node_modules`, `@types/react` and TypeScript's `lib.*.d.ts` are told apart, `\` is read as `/`): `apps/oracle/src/path-class.ts` and `scripts/oracle_data.py` read it, and `apps/oracle/tests/path-class.test.ts` and `scripts/test_path_classes.py` run the same cases of `apps/oracle/tests/fixtures/path-class-cases.json`. `scripts/rdt.mjs` reads it too, to leave `@types/react`'s props out of its dump. A function Caliper itself reports as a component stays in the universe whatever its shape. A default export is named from its declaration (`export default function Foo` is `Foo`; one with no name of its own takes its file's, PascalCased, as Caliper names it), which is how it meets Caliper's and RDT's entries. A component is its declaration, not an export name: `export default function Foo` followed by `export { Foo }` or `export { Foo as Bar }` is one component, counted once under the declaration's own name, and a re-export (`export { Foo } from './Foo'`, `export *`) is counted only in the file that declares it, never in the importing file; two components of one name in different files are two (`declaredExports` in `apps/oracle/src/checker-components.ts`, which both the oracle and the reference universe read). The universe still holds some functions that are not components, because the rules read shape and not intent, so read the shares as a comparison between tools, not as a share of real components. For each tool the record has, in `oracle.tools`:
124:- **Agreement of the whole universe** (`agree_universe`): identical or spelled, over every prop in the universe. A prop the tool omits counts against it. This is the comparison between tools; Caliper's own headline is below.
141:### The headline
143:What matters is whether the types Storybook and agents are shown are right, not whether Caliper matches RDT. The headline (`scripts/headline.py`, read from `oracle.tools.caliper_reported`, which `apps/oracle/src/tool-score.ts` `scoreReported` computes) takes every own prop the checker finds on a component Caliper reports, so a function the checker takes for a component and Caliper rightly ignores does not count against it, and sorts each prop into one kind:
149:- **Not judged**: the oracle did not evaluate the checker's type, so nothing was compared. It is in none of correct, less precise or wrong, and is outside the judged props the gate divides by.
151:- **Named only**: Caliper lists the prop by name as a member of a collapsed inheritance layer, so it is surfaced but a reader sees no type for it. It is counted apart, as neither correct nor wrong, because correct values reached through a layer are a win and a bare name is not.
153:The record keeps the counts per corpus as `headline`, next to the unchanged `oracle` and `recall` fields. The shares in the summary are of every prop of the components Caliper reports. The gate uses the wrong share of the props whose type can be judged (correct, less precise and wrong), so a corpus with many layer-only props does not dilute it.
159:- a whole run is over its corpus's budget, with dependencies loaded, the default (`BUDGETS` in `scripts/headline.py`; "The budgets" above). The budgets are user-facing limits, not week-over-week ones; the structural resolver's, 2 s and 600 MiB, were never reached (Chakra, the largest corpus, ran in 0.24 s and 378 MiB in the weekly run of 2026-11-06). Only Caliper's own figure for that corpus is read: RDT's and react-docgen's time and memory are references, shown in the table and never in the issue. A peak that is the same to the MiB for Caliper, RDT and react-docgen on one corpus is not read at all (`own_peak` in `scripts/headline.py`): three tools never peak together, so it is one process-wide maximum, which is what the weekly record of 2026-11-02 held (1901 MiB for shadcn, antd and spectrum, every tool), before the helper read each run's own peak. Its first issue (#279) reported that figure and, as its comment, time rises of 11 to 33% on a median of five runs between two records, which the 10% rule of that week read as getting worse; the rule now opens nothing for them (`changes` lists them in the summary).
161:Recall against RDT stays information. A local run on antd and shadcn at the commit that added this, with the default collapse, reads: antd 83.7% correct, 6.0% less precise, 0.00% wrong, 10.2% named only (3,426 props); shadcn 54.4% correct, 5.1% less precise, 0.06% wrong (0.096% of the judged props, just under the gate), 0.4% missing, 39.6% named only (13,918 props). The weekly record collapses nothing (`--collapse-inherited-props none`), so named only is 0 there; its run of 2026-11-06 reads antd 94.0% correct, 6.0% less precise, 0 wrong, and shadcn 93.8% correct, 5.3% less precise, 8 wrong (0.058% of the shared props), 0.4% missing (`headline` in `weekly.json`, `main` at `c5fbb33e`). Mantine, Chakra and Spectrum read in that run: 90.9%, 100.0% and 83.7% agree, with 0, 1 and 22 wrong. Of Spectrum's 22, the comparator's index-signature artifact accounts for all (`docs/rdt-differences.md`), so that gate firing is false until the comparator is corrected.
163:**What changed with `oracle.universe_version` 4: an unjudged comparison is scored apart from agreement.** The comparison returned `identical` whenever the checker side was opaque (a type the normalizer cut at the depth limit or has no reader for), so those props counted as agreement. They are now `not judged` (`oracle.verdicts['not judged']`, `tools.*.verdicts['not judged']`, a column of the headline table, and `headline.not_judged`). `shared_props`, `agree` and `wrong` keep their formulas, over the props both tools list: a not judged prop is in `shared_props` and in neither `agree` nor `wrong`. The numbers on the next weekly run therefore change: `agree` falls, the correct share of the headline falls, and the wrong share of the judged props can rise slightly because the judged props are fewer, by as many props as were opaque on the checker side, which has not been measured (this change was not run against the corpora). The weekly does not compare version 4 with a record of version 3, so that first move opens no issue. The construct suite shows the size of it on 4 of its fixtures: through the checker path `generics/19-recursive-json`, `react/16-ref`, `react/27-sx-object` and `react/30-dispatch-setstate` read `identical` against goldens cut at the depth limit, and read `not judged` now (`apps/oracle/construct-suite/checker-expectations.json`). Two smaller moves ride with it: the reference of the next section no longer takes an unevaluated checker type as a reference (the declaration stands alone, or the prop has no reference), and the oracle's three copies of "is this path `@types/react`" and "is this path a dependency" are one rule (`apps/oracle/src/path-classes.json`), which reads an `@types/react` directory outside `node_modules` as the project's own and a Windows path as its POSIX spelling.

# oracle counts.
UNIVERSE_VERSION = 5
# No single measured command runs longer than this (seconds): a hung one is killed and its corpus recorded as failed.
STEP_TIMEOUT = 2400


class StepFailed(Exception):
    """A command of one corpus's measurement that did not finish well: `step` names it, `code` is its exit status
    (negative for a signal, None for a timeout) and `tail` the last 20 lines of its stderr."""

    def __init__(self, step, message, code=None, tail=''):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.step = step
        self.code = code
        self.tail = tail


def log(message):
    print(message, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)


def step(label, command, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=None):
    """`run_once` of one measured command, logging its exit status and wall time to stderr; a command that fails is a
    StepFailed naming `label`."""
    start = time.monotonic()
    try:
        result = run_once(command, stdout=stdout, timeout=STEP_TIMEOUT if timeout is None else timeout)
    except corpora.RunFailed as error:
        log(f'{label}: exit {error.code if error.code is not None else "none"} after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s: {error}')
        raise StepFailed(label, str(error), error.code, error.tail) from error
    log(f'{label}: exit 0 after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s')
    return result


def capture(label, command, timeout=None):
    """The stdout of a command that must succeed, logged like `step`."""
    start = time.monotonic()
    try:
        done = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, errors='replace',
                              timeout=STEP_TIMEOUT if timeout is None else timeout)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:
        log(f'{label}: timed out after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s')
        raise StepFailed(label, f'{label} ran past its {error.timeout} s timeout and was killed') from error
    except OSError as error:
        log(f'{label}: cannot run: {error}')
        raise StepFailed(label, f'{label}: cannot run: {error}', 127) from error
    log(f'{label}: exit {done.returncode} after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s')
    if done.returncode != 0:
        raise StepFailed(label, f'{label} exited with {done.returncode}', done.returncode,
                         '\n'.join(done.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-20:]))
    return done.stdout


def norm_name(name):
    """A component name as the tools may spell it: no `(file)` suffix, namespace or punctuation."""
    name = re.sub(r' \(.*\)$', '', name).split('/')[-1].split('.')[-1]
    return re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]', '', name.lower())


def relative(path, root):
    """`path` relative to `root`, both through symlinks: Caliper reports canonical paths, RDT the ones it was given."""
    return os.path.relpath(os.path.realpath(path), os.path.realpath(root))


def program_inputs(name, src, out_dir):
    """The component files (every `.tsx` under the source directory) and a tsconfig rooted there."""
    files = []
    for current, dirs, names in os.walk(src):
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d != 'node_modules']
        files += [os.path.join(current, n) for n in names if n.endswith('.tsx')]
    list_file = os.path.join(out_dir, f'{name}.files.txt')
    with open(list_file, 'w') as f:
        f.write('\n'.join(sorted(files)) + '\n')
    tsconfig = os.path.join(out_dir, f'{name}.tsconfig.json')
    with open(tsconfig, 'w') as f:
        json.dump({
            'include': [f'{src}/**/*.ts', f'{src}/**/*.tsx'],
            'compilerOptions': {'target': 'ES2022', 'module': 'ESNext', 'moduleResolution': 'bundler', 'jsx': 'react-jsx',
                                'strict': True, 'skipLibCheck': True, 'noEmit': True},
        }, f, indent=2)
    return list_file, tsconfig


def tool_run(command, out, label='tool'):
    """One whole run of a Node tool that writes its components to `out`: wall ms, peak RSS MiB and the components."""
    seconds, rss = step(label, command)
    with open(out) as f:
        return {'ms': round(seconds * 1000), 'rss_mib': round(rss)}, json.load(f)['components']


def caliper_run(binary, src, runs, label='Caliper'):
    """Median wall ms and largest peak RSS MiB of `extract --json` in the Storybook addon's configuration (dependencies
    loaded, `--collapse-inherited-props dependencies` pinned: the addon's default), and the JSON's size. The checker answers, as
    it does by default (docs/measurement.md). The parse caches are warm (a warm-up run fills them), but each timed run
    asks the checker everything: the answer `extract` keeps is removed first, since react-docgen-typescript keeps none.
    `rerun_ms` is the median of as many runs that find it, what a rerun over unchanged files costs."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as cache, tempfile.TemporaryFile() as out:
        command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'dependencies',
                   '--cache-dir', cache]
        step(f'{label} warm-up', command, stdout=out)
        size = out.tell()
        kept = os.path.join(cache, 'checker-answers.msgpack')
        samples = []
        for _ in range(runs):
            if os.path.exists(kept):
                os.remove(kept)
            samples.append(step(f'{label} run {len(samples) + 1}', command))
        reruns = [step(f'{label} rerun {i + 1}', command) for i in range(runs)]
    return {'ms': round(statistics.median(s for s, _ in samples) * 1000), 'rss_mib': round(max(r for _, r in samples)),
            'json_mb': round(size / 2**20, 2), 'rerun_ms': round(statistics.median(s for s, _ in reruns) * 1000)}


def caliper_components(binary, src, root, label='Caliper components'):
    """Caliper's components in RDT's format, as (file, name) -> prop names."""
    command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--format', 'rdt', '--html-attributes', 'full', '--include-unexported',
               '--quiet', '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'none']
    out = capture(label, command)
    return {(relative(c['filePath'], root), norm_name(c['displayName'])): set(c['props'])
            for c in json.loads(out[out.index('{'):]).values()}


def caliper_layer_members(binary, src, root, label='Caliper layers'):
    """The props Caliper's collapsed inheritance layers hold, as (file, name) -> prop names: the output names them in a
    layer instead of listing them as props, and the canonical JSON is the one that carries the layers."""
    command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--html-attributes', 'full', '--include-unexported', '--quiet',
               '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'none']
    out = capture(label, command)
    document = schema_version.check(json.loads(out[out.index('{'):]), 'weekly')
    lists = document.get('nameLists', {})
    members = {}
    for c in document['components'].values():
        names = set()
        for layer in c.get('inheritance', []):
            if layer.get('members'):
                names |= set(lists[layer['members']])
        members[(relative(c['filePath'], root), norm_name(c['displayName']))] = names
    return members


# The shape rules of `exclusion`, shared with the oracle's universe (apps/oracle/src/component-shape.ts): the patterns are in
# one file both read (scripts/oracle_data.py), and both run the cases of apps/oracle/tests/fixtures/component-shape-cases.json.
HOOK = re.compile(oracle_data.SHAPE['hook'])
PROMISE_TYPE = re.compile(oracle_data.SHAPE['promiseType'])
EXTENSIONS = ('', '.tsx', '.ts', '/index.tsx', '/index.ts')
# An identifier inside any number of calls (`memo(forwardRef(Foo))`, `React.memo(Foo)`, `Object.assign(Foo, {...})`),
# followed by what ends an argument or an expression: `, ) ; !`, a type assertion or the end of the line.
WRAPPED = r'(?:[\w.]+\s*(?:<[^>]*>)?\s*\(\s*)*(\w+)(?=\s*[,);!]|\s+as\b|\s+satisfies\b|\s*$)'


def declared_in_react(info):
    return oracle_data.is_react_types(info.get('parent') or '')


def exclusion(comp):
    """Why RDT's entry is not a component, from what RDT reports about it, or None. RDT lists every function it can
    give a parameter to, so hooks, route handlers, helpers and context objects come with it. The evidence is the shape:
    props that are the members of a TypeScript lib type (`String`, `Function`, `Request`) mean the parameter is not an
    object of props; a hook is named `use` and a capital; a `value` declared by `@types/react` and nothing else is a
    context's Provider; a lowercase name cannot be a JSX tag unless it takes the attributes of one (a `@types/react`
    prop) or is the file's or directory's own name, which RDT gives a default export; and props that are all promises
    are handed over by a router, not by a parent. The oracle's universe applies the same rules to the checker's functions
    (apps/oracle/src/component-shape.ts)."""
    props = comp['props']
    in_lib = sum(oracle_data.is_lib_file(i.get('parent') or '') for i in props.values())
    if in_lib * 2 > len(props):
        return 'lib_members'
    name = comp['name']
    if HOOK.search(name):
        return 'hook'

# oracle counts.
UNIVERSE_VERSION = 5
# No single measured command runs longer than this (seconds): a hung one is killed and its corpus recorded as failed.
STEP_TIMEOUT = 2400


class StepFailed(Exception):
    """A command of one corpus's measurement that did not finish well: `step` names it, `code` is its exit status
    (negative for a signal, None for a timeout) and `tail` the last 20 lines of its stderr."""

    def __init__(self, step, message, code=None, tail=''):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.step = step
        self.code = code
        self.tail = tail


def log(message):
    print(message, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)


def step(label, command, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=None):
    """`run_once` of one measured command, logging its exit status and wall time to stderr; a command that fails is a
    StepFailed naming `label`."""
    start = time.monotonic()
    try:
        result = run_once(command, stdout=stdout, timeout=STEP_TIMEOUT if timeout is None else timeout)
    except corpora.RunFailed as error:
        log(f'{label}: exit {error.code if error.code is not None else "none"} after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s: {error}')
        raise StepFailed(label, str(error), error.code, error.tail) from error
    log(f'{label}: exit 0 after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s')
    return result


def capture(label, command, timeout=None):
    """The stdout of a command that must succeed, logged like `step`."""
    start = time.monotonic()
    try:
        done = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, errors='replace',
                              timeout=STEP_TIMEOUT if timeout is None else timeout)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:
        log(f'{label}: timed out after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s')
        raise StepFailed(label, f'{label} ran past its {error.timeout} s timeout and was killed') from error
    except OSError as error:
        log(f'{label}: cannot run: {error}')
        raise StepFailed(label, f'{label}: cannot run: {error}', 127) from error
    log(f'{label}: exit {done.returncode} after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s')
    if done.returncode != 0:
        raise StepFailed(label, f'{label} exited with {done.returncode}', done.returncode,
                         '\n'.join(done.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-20:]))
    return done.stdout


def norm_name(name):
    """A component name as the tools may spell it: no `(file)` suffix, namespace or punctuation."""
    name = re.sub(r' \(.*\)$', '', name).split('/')[-1].split('.')[-1]
    return re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]', '', name.lower())


def relative(path, root):
    """`path` relative to `root`, both through symlinks: Caliper reports canonical paths, RDT the ones it was given."""
    return os.path.relpath(os.path.realpath(path), os.path.realpath(root))


def program_inputs(name, src, out_dir):
    """The component files (every `.tsx` under the source directory) and a tsconfig rooted there."""
    files = []
    for current, dirs, names in os.walk(src):
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d != 'node_modules']
        files += [os.path.join(current, n) for n in names if n.endswith('.tsx')]
    list_file = os.path.join(out_dir, f'{name}.files.txt')
    with open(list_file, 'w') as f:
        f.write('\n'.join(sorted(files)) + '\n')
    tsconfig = os.path.join(out_dir, f'{name}.tsconfig.json')
    with open(tsconfig, 'w') as f:
        json.dump({
            'include': [f'{src}/**/*.ts', f'{src}/**/*.tsx'],
            'compilerOptions': {'target': 'ES2022', 'module': 'ESNext', 'moduleResolution': 'bundler', 'jsx': 'react-jsx',
                                'strict': True, 'skipLibCheck': True, 'noEmit': True},
        }, f, indent=2)

def tool_run(command, out, label='tool'):
    """One whole run of a Node tool that writes its components to `out`: wall ms, peak RSS MiB and the components."""
    seconds, rss = step(label, command)
    with open(out) as f:
        return {'ms': round(seconds * 1000), 'rss_mib': round(rss)}, json.load(f)['components']


def caliper_run(binary, src, runs, label='Caliper'):
    """Median wall ms and largest peak RSS MiB of `extract --json` in the Storybook addon's configuration (dependencies
    loaded, `--collapse-inherited-props dependencies` pinned: the addon's default), and the JSON's size. The checker answers, as
    it does by default (docs/measurement.md). The parse caches are warm (a warm-up run fills them), but each timed run
    asks the checker everything: the answer `extract` keeps is removed first, since react-docgen-typescript keeps none.
    `rerun_ms` is the median of as many runs that find it, what a rerun over unchanged files costs."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as cache, tempfile.TemporaryFile() as out:
        command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'dependencies',
                   '--cache-dir', cache]
        step(f'{label} warm-up', command, stdout=out)
        size = out.tell()
        kept = os.path.join(cache, 'checker-answers.msgpack')
        samples = []
        for _ in range(runs):
            if os.path.exists(kept):
                os.remove(kept)
            samples.append(step(f'{label} run {len(samples) + 1}', command))
        reruns = [step(f'{label} rerun {i + 1}', command) for i in range(runs)]
    return {'ms': round(statistics.median(s for s, _ in samples) * 1000), 'rss_mib': round(max(r for _, r in samples)),
            'json_mb': round(size / 2**20, 2), 'rerun_ms': round(statistics.median(s for s, _ in reruns) * 1000)}

def recall(items, found, layered=None):
    """Against the reference: the components the tool also reports and, of those, RDT's props it lists, apart from and
    with `@types/react`'s, so a missing component and a missing prop are counted once each. `own` and `react` count the
    props listed as props; `own_layers` and `react_layers` also count those held in a collapsed layer (`layered`), which
    the output names without listing them."""
    layered = layered or {}
    count = {'components': [0, 0], 'own': [0, 0], 'react': [0, 0], 'own_layers': [0, 0], 'react_layers': [0, 0]}
    for item in items:
        count['components'][1] += 1
        key = next((k for k in item['keys'] if k in found), None)
        if key is None:
            continue
        in_layers = layered.get(key, set())
        count['components'][0] += 1
        for prop, kind in item['props'].items():
            count[kind][1] += 1
            count[kind][0] += prop in found[key]
            count[f'{kind}_layers'][1] += 1
            count[f'{kind}_layers'][0] += prop in found[key] or prop in in_layers
    return count


def rate(pair):
    return pair[0] / pair[1] if pair[1] else 0.0


def oracle_tools(tools):
    """The oracle's score for each tool, without the examples that are there to review the adapters by."""
    return {tool: {key: value for key, value in score.items() if key != 'examples'} for tool, score in tools.items()}


def oracle(binary, name, src, root, work, rdt_out, rdg_out):
    """How often TypeScript 7.1's checker contradicts Caliper's prop types (apps/oracle/src/oracle.ts), and how RDT and
    react-docgen fare against it over the same props. `shared_props`, `agree` and `wrong` are Caliper's, over the props
    both list, and keep their meaning from week to week (a prop the checker side did not evaluate is in `shared_props`
    and counts toward neither `agree` nor `wrong`, as `verdicts['not judged']`); `tools` holds all three over every prop of the candidate
    components the checker finds (the functions `exclusion`'s shape rules take out are left out: `universe_excluded`), and
    `tools_all_functions` the same scores over every function the checker takes for a component, as `tools` was before
    `universe_version` 2."""
    caliper_json = os.path.join(work, f'{name}.caliper.json')
    with open(caliper_json, 'w') as f:
        subprocess.run([binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--html-attributes', 'full', '--include-unexported',
                        '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'none', '--quiet'],
                       stdout=f, check=True)

def recall(items, found, layered=None):
    """Against the reference: the components the tool also reports and, of those, RDT's props it lists, apart from and
    with `@types/react`'s, so a missing component and a missing prop are counted once each. `own` and `react` count the
    props listed as props; `own_layers` and `react_layers` also count those held in a collapsed layer (`layered`), which
    the output names without listing them."""
    layered = layered or {}
    count = {'components': [0, 0], 'own': [0, 0], 'react': [0, 0], 'own_layers': [0, 0], 'react_layers': [0, 0]}
    for item in items:
        count['components'][1] += 1
        key = next((k for k in item['keys'] if k in found), None)
        if key is None:
            continue
        in_layers = layered.get(key, set())
        count['components'][0] += 1
        for prop, kind in item['props'].items():
            count[kind][1] += 1
            count[kind][0] += prop in found[key]
            count[f'{kind}_layers'][1] += 1
            count[f'{kind}_layers'][0] += prop in found[key] or prop in in_layers
    return count

    return pair[0] / pair[1] if pair[1] else 0.0

def measure(args, corpus, work):
    root = os.path.join(os.path.abspath(args.corpora), corpus['clone'])
    src = corpora.ready(corpus, os.path.abspath(args.corpora), sparse=False)
    if not src:
        raise StepFailed('setup', f"{corpus['name']}: not installed; run `scripts/corpora.py setup` first")
    list_file, tsconfig = program_inputs(corpus['name'], src, work)
    print(f"{corpus['name']}: RDT", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    rdt_out = os.path.join(work, f"{corpus['name']}.rdt.json")
    rdt, rdt_components = tool_run(['node', '--max-old-space-size=8192', os.path.join(ROOT, 'scripts', 'rdt.mjs'),
                                    list_file, tsconfig, rdt_out], rdt_out,
                                   f"{corpus['name']} RDT")
    print(f"{corpus['name']}: react-docgen", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    rdg_out = os.path.join(work, f"{corpus['name']}.rdg.json")
    rdg, rdg_components = tool_run(['node', os.path.join(ROOT, 'scripts', 'rdg.mjs'), list_file, rdg_out], rdg_out,
                                   f"{corpus['name']} react-docgen")
    print(f"{corpus['name']}: Caliper", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    found = {(relative(c['file'], root), norm_name(c['name'])): set(c['props']) for c in rdg_components}
    caliper_found = caliper_components(args.bin, src, root, f"{corpus['name']} Caliper components")
    items, counts = reference(rdt_components, caliper_found, root)
    entry = {
        'commit': corpus['commit'],
        'caliper': caliper_run(args.bin, src, args.runs, f"{corpus['name']} Caliper"),
        'rdt': rdt,
        'react_docgen': rdg,
        'reference': counts,
        'recall': {'caliper': recall(items, caliper_found, caliper_layer_members(args.bin, src, root, f"{corpus['name']} Caliper layers")),
                   'react_docgen': recall(items, found)},
    }
    if args.oracle:
        try:
            entry['oracle'] = oracle(args.bin, corpus['name'], src, root, work, rdt_out, rdg_out)
            if h := headline.compute(entry['oracle']):
                entry['headline'] = h
        except (subprocess.SubprocessError, OSError, KeyError) as error:
            entry['oracle'] = {'error': str(error)}
    if args.agent_eval:
        try:
            result = agent_eval.evaluate(args.bin, corpus['name'], src, root, tsconfig, work)
            if result:
                entry['agent_eval'] = result
        except (subprocess.SubprocessError, OSError, KeyError, ValueError) as error:
            entry['agent_eval'] = {'error': str(error)}
    return entry

def run_once(args, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=None):
    """Wall seconds and peak RSS in MiB of one process, measured by a small helper process so that this process's own
    memory never leaks into the number. A helper that fails, a result it did not write, a command that cannot run, that
    exits non-zero or dies of a signal, and one that runs past `timeout` seconds (it and its helper are killed) are each
    a RunFailed saying what happened, with the end of the helper's stderr."""
    command = ' '.join(args)
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile('r', suffix='.json') as result:
        helper = [sys.executable, '-I', os.path.abspath(__file__), 'measure', result.name, '--'] + list(args)
        # Its own session, so that a timeout can kill the measured command with it, not only the helper.
        process = subprocess.Popen(helper, stdout=stdout, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, errors='replace',
                                   start_new_session=True)
        try:
            _, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            try:
                os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
            except ProcessLookupError:
                pass
            _, stderr = process.communicate()
            raise RunFailed(f'{command} ran past its {timeout} s timeout and was killed', tail=stderr) from None
        detail = stderr.strip()[-500:]
        if process.returncode != 0:
            raise RunFailed(f'the measuring helper failed (exit {process.returncode}) running {command}: {detail}',
                            process.returncode, stderr)
        try:
            seconds, rss, code = json.load(result)
        except ValueError as error:
            raise RunFailed(f'the measuring helper wrote no result for {command}: {error}', tail=stderr) from error
    if code != 0:
        raise RunFailed(f'{command} exited with {code}' + (f': {detail}' if detail else ''), code, stderr)
    return seconds, rss


def package_manager_env(base):
    caches = os.path.join(base, 'caches')
    # corepack downloads CommonJS bundles (yarn 4's `yarn.js`). Its home lives under this repository, whose root
    # package.json says `"type": "module"`, so Node would load them as ES modules, where `require` does not exist.
    corepack_home = os.path.join(caches, 'corepack')
    os.makedirs(corepack_home, exist_ok=True)
    with open(os.path.join(corepack_home, 'package.json'), 'w') as manifest:
        manifest.write('{"type": "commonjs"}\n')
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.update({
        'COREPACK_HOME': corepack_home,
        'COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT': '0',
        'COREPACK_ENABLE_AUTO_PIN': '0',
        'YARN_CACHE_FOLDER': os.path.join(caches, 'yarn'),
        'YARN_GLOBAL_FOLDER': os.path.join(caches, 'yarn-global'),
        'YARN_ENABLE_GLOBAL_CACHE': '0',
        'YARN_ENABLE_SCRIPTS': '0',
        'YARN_NODE_LINKER': 'node-modules',
        'YARN_ENABLE_TELEMETRY': '0',
        'npm_config_cache': os.path.join(caches, 'npm'),
        'PATH': os.path.join(base, 'tools', 'bin') + os.pathsep + os.environ.get('PATH', ''),
    def test_the_record_counts_every_cause_and_caps_the_lists(self):
        rdt = [comp(f'N{i}', {'a': prop()}, f'{self.root}/src/plain/Plain.tsx') for i in range(weekly.LIST_CAP + 3)]
        _, stats = weekly.reference(rdt, {}, self.root)
        self.assertEqual(stats['unmatched']['by_cause'], {'file_without_components': weekly.LIST_CAP + 3})
        self.assertEqual(len(stats['unmatched']['listed']['file_without_components']), weekly.LIST_CAP)
